text: Within the last few years, City staff have undertaken two speed hump feasibility studies on Brock Avenue (Dundas Street West to Florence Street), but the installation criteria have not been met. Subsequently, a City poll was undertaken in the fall of 2015 to determine resident support for speed humps on Brock Avenue; however, the minimum response rate of (50% + 1) was not met. Of the residents that responded, over 60% supported the idea of speed humps on Brock Avenue. Given the negative poll results, the speed humps could not be installed. Residents have continued to request that speed humps be installed due to the presence of a highly used community centre, arena and school walking route. I informed them that I would need a strong resident petition in order to move a motion to have speed humps installed. I have since received this petition and I am by way of this motion requesting that…

The Toronto and East York Community Council: 1. Directed the City Solicitor to prepare a by-law to alter the roadway to install six speed humps on Brock Avenue, between Dundas Street West and Florence Street, generally as shown on the attached Drawing No. 421G-1757, dated April 2015 attached to the Letter (May 2, 2018) from Councillor Ana Bailão.
